title: Mandela's long walk
summary: Nelson Mandela's life traced from a rural Eastern Cape village to the presidency, through 27 years in prison. It follows the arc of the struggle against apartheid itself.
caveat: This is one of the best-documented lives in South African history: Mandela's own autobiography, an authorised biography, court records and press coverage agree on nearly every place and date here.

stops.title: Born in Mvezo
stops.narration: Rolihlahla Mandela was born in this village on the Mbashe River, into a branch of the Thembu royal family. His father lost his position as headman when Mandela was an infant, and the family moved.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)

stops.title: Childhood in Qunu
stops.narration: Mandela grew up herding cattle in Qunu and was given the name Nelson by a teacher at the local mission school. After his father died, he went to live under the guardianship of the Thembu regent, Jongintaba.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: University of Fort Hare
stops.narration: Fort Hare was one of the few universities open to Black South Africans, and Mandela met Oliver Tambo here. He left in 1940 after joining a student protest and refusing to back down.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Arrives in Johannesburg
stops.narration: Fleeing an arranged marriage, Mandela came to Johannesburg and lived in Alexandra township while working and studying law. Walter Sisulu helped him find work and drew him into the African National Congress.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)

stops.title: 8115 Vilakazi Street
stops.narration: Mandela moved into this small house in Orlando West, his home until his arrest. In 1952 he helped lead the Defiance Campaign and opened South Africa's first Black law firm with Tambo.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Arrested near Howick
stops.narration: After 17 months underground, Mandela was stopped at a police roadblock while disguised as a chauffeur. A sculpture of 50 steel columns now marks the capture site beside the road.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows Howick; the capture site is just outside the town.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Liliesleaf Farm raid
stops.narration: Police raided this farm, the secret headquarters of the ANC's armed wing, and seized documents that put Mandela, already in prison, on trial with the movement's leadership.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: The Rivonia Trial
stops.narration: From the dock, Mandela said democracy and freedom were "an ideal for which I am prepared to die". He and seven others were sentenced to life imprisonment in June.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Robben Island
stops.narration: Prisoner 466/64 spent 18 years here, breaking rocks in a lime quarry that damaged his eyes. The island became known as "the university": prisoners taught each other in secret.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)

stops.title: Pollsmoor Prison
stops.narration: Mandela was moved to the mainland with other senior leaders. From here, in 1985, he began secret talks with the government without telling his comrades.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Victor Verster Prison
stops.narration: His last years in prison were spent in a warder's cottage here, where talks with the government continued. He walked out of its gates on 11 February 1990.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)

stops.title: Speech from City Hall
stops.narration: Hours after his release, Mandela spoke from the balcony of City Hall to a crowd on the Grand Parade. He had been in prison for 27 years.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Inauguration
stops.narration: After the first election open to all South Africans, Mandela was sworn in as president at the Union Buildings, the seat of the government that had imprisoned him.
sources: Nelson Mandela, Long Walk to Freedom (1994)
Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)

stops.title: Laid to rest in Qunu
stops.narration: Mandela died on 5 December 2013, aged 95, and was buried in the village where he grew up.
sources: Anthony Sampson, Mandela: The Authorised Biography (1999)
